title: 2AM Stabilization Diary — autoscaler anomaly
body:
Purpose:
This is a short, messy stabilization diary captured live during the 02:00–04:30 window. The goal is to record what we tried, why we tried it, and what still needs follow-up. Treat everything here as ephemeral notes; formal incident writeup to follow in INF-7421.

Situation summary (TL;DR):
- Starting ~01:50 UTC, we saw repeated timeouts for short tail latency on the hosted API (text/generate).
- Root cause hypothesis at 03:00: autoscaler over-triggered scale-downs on a subset of GPU pools (pool: inference-pool-eu-west-1b) when the new continuous-batching heuristic mis-classified a burst as idle. Pods went to Terminating and did not reattach quickly due to a KV-cache warmup hitch.
- Impact: short 200–500ms spikes turned into 3–12s p50/p90 spikes for routes using models/redwood-compat/opt-2.7b-q8. Customer-facing errors were 502/504 from the inference-proxy.

What I observed (chronological):
- 01:48: Alerts: route-text-generate p95 > 2s (alert SRE-LAT-013).
- 01:52: CI/Telemetry: spikes correlated with increases in scale-down events from the autoscaler-controller (controller logs show "no recent requests, scale down" while proxy metrics show ongoing requests with small batch sizes).
- 02:05: Noticed high KV cache miss ratio on model-redwood-compat-2.7b; cache warming times ~1.6s per warm start.
- 02:12: Attempted to patch autoscaler to be more conservative (temp): increase min_replicas for inference-pool-eu-west-1b from 2 -> 3. Patch ID: patch-autoscaler-eu-20251107-1 (applied via kustomize overlay).
- 02:18: Latency improved marginally but a second wave hit at 02:30 when controller logic retried scale-down during a small window of low batch fill.
- 02:40: Rolled back the autoscaler heuristic change that landed today in PR #391 (git revert + force-deploy) to restore previous stable behavior.
- 03:06: Restored cache priming script in deployment init (we had disabled priming for a roll two hours prior).
- 03:22: Stabilized to p95 ~1.2s across routes. Slow tail still intermittent.

Quick checklist of live actions performed (commands & outcomes):
- Check pods and recent restarts: kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=inference-pool-eu-west-1b; found 3 pod restarts between 01:40–02:10.
- Inspect autoscaler controller logs: kubectl -n control logs deploy/autoscaler-controller --since=4h | rg "scaleDown" -- context: saw repeated "scaleDown triggered by idle heuristic" close to bursts.
- Revert PR: git revert 9f2a4b3 (realtime-autoscaler) && ./deploy/deploy.sh k8s/eu-west-1b --tag=stable-20251106 -> deployment succeeded.
- Bump min replicas: kubectl -n inference apply -f overlays/eu-west/min-replicas-3.yaml (applied) — note: this is a temporary guard, not a long-term config.
- Re-enable cache priming: update configmap inference-init -> set PRIMING_ENABLED=true and restart daemonset (rolled).

Temporary mitigation policy (what I left in place):
- min_replicas for inference-pool-eu-west-1b = 3 (temp guard). Owner: oncall (Ravi). TODO remove after analysis and load-testing (ticket INF-7421).
- Autoscaler heuristic revert is currently deployed to eu-west-1b only. Global revert pending until full regression test.
- Cache priming re-enabled on critical model groups (redwood-compat-*).

Immediate follow-ups (owners & rough ETA):
- SRE: run controlled load test against the reverted autoscaler to validate stable behavior under burst traffic (Liam, ETA 2025-11-08 EOD).
- Runtime team: add a KV-cache metric export for warmup time and expose per-model warm rate (Ava, ETA 2025-11-10).
- Product: notify customers with high SLA expectations that we had transient degradation and that mitigations are in place (Customer Success owns comms; assigned to Priya – see INF-7421).
- Engineering: add a canary gating step to autoscaler PRs that simulates high small-batch traffic (owner: runtime/serving; ETA 2025-11-17).

Commands / diagnostics to run next shift (copy/paste):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=inference-pool-eu-west-1b -o wide
- kubectl -n control logs deploy/autoscaler-controller --since=2h | rg "scaleDown|scaleUp|idle heuristic"
- redwood-cli metrics query "model:kv_cache_warmup_seconds{model=\"redwood-compat-2.7b\"}" --since 4h
- curl -sS https://status-api.internal.redwood/v1/route-stats?route=text.generate | jq . | less

Known unknowns / hypotheses (short):
- Hypothesis A: the new batchiness heuristic relies on a short-term moving average that undercounts low-rate bursts, causing scale-downs to happen even though request inter-arrival is non-uniform.
- Hypothesis B: cache priming disabled earlier exposed a cold-start penalty that interacts poorly with the autoscaler; without priming, new pods ramp slower and miss early requests, amplifying client-facing latency.
- Unknown: exact interaction window between kube terminating grace period and our proxy's request draining. Need to validate drain settings.

Escalation list and contacts (short):
- On-call infra lead: Ava Chen (pager: +1-415-555-0132 / Slack @ava)
- Runtime owner: Miguel Santos (Slack @miguel, GH: @msantos)
- Customer ops: Priya Desai (Slack @priya-cs)

What I would do differently next time (notes to self):
- Don't disable cache priming in a global deploy without a compensating autoscaler guard.
- Add a temporary traffic-capture on proxy when we revert autoscaler changes to record small-batch patterns for 24h.
- Make min_replicas changes via a staged rollout (one AZ -> monitor -> global).

Open todos I left in the cluster (do before next day shift):
- Create a lightweight metric dashboard for "kv-cache warmups per pod" and alert if >30% of new pods experience warmup > 1s (ticket INF-7422).
- Add an annotation on the autoscaler deployment documenting the revert and link to INF-7421.
- Toggle off the temporary min_replicas guard once we validate autoscaler fixes in a canary.

Random scribbles / breadcrumbs (for follow up):
- Controller log excerpt saved to /tmp/autoscaler-snip-20251107.log on oncall VM.
- Local load script: tools/loaders/small-batch-spike.py (used by Liam to reproduce).

Closing note: the system is not "fixed" yet — we've stabilized behavior and reduced customer-impact, but the underlying interplay between autoscaler heuristics and cache warmups needs a concrete mitigant. This diary should help whoever picks up the morning shift to quickly reproduce, continue the investigation, and prioritize a permanent fix.

Ravi
2:45 AM — stabilization diary snapshot
